description: Greatest common factor and least common multiple of any list.

faqs.a: With Euclid's algorithm applied pairwise across the list: GCF(a,b,c) = GCF(GCF(a,b),c), and LCM uses the identity LCM(a,b) = |a×b| ÷ GCF(a,b).
faqs.q: How are GCF and LCM computed?

faqs.a: Signs are ignored — both are computed on absolute values. Zeros are skipped for GCF; a zero in the list makes the LCM zero.
faqs.q: How are negative numbers and zeros handled?

faqs.a: Yes, up to 100 integers. Very large values may lose precision because the LCM is computed in floating point.
faqs.q: How many numbers can I enter?

howto: Type integers separated by commas, spaces or new lines.
Read the GCF and LCM plus how many numbers were used.
Edit the list any time — results update on demand.
